findings.claim: The first FULL-VIEWPORT byte-exact gate is blocked by a frame-capture mismatch, NOT a decoder gap. The committed engine oracle maze-corridor.idx.gz is the gy=121 facing-0 view (party 3 cells PAST the portcullis gate; small far colored window — viewport idx hist {0:4005,1:743,5:5,8:6698,9:8179,10:79,13:3}; ZERO wt=2 wall spans per maze-frames.json wt2_depthFields=[] — so it is ENTIRELY OR-blit background). The OR-blit can only be live-captured on the PATCHED trace core, which (a) CANNOT unserialize the committed gy=121 .state.gz (DBPSerialize_CPU layout divergence — err unser, confirmed again this run on both maze-corridor.state.gz and the uncompressed tools/libretro/states/maze-corridor.state), and (b) a fresh patched-core drive lands at gy=118 (party AT the gate; large colored window — different view, decode(its bg-oracle) vs committed maze-corridor viewport = 58.08%) and CANNOT advance past the gate to gy=121 (the gate-traversal is a navigation/timing state the fresh forward-walk recipe does not reproduce — gy plateaus at 118-119). So no committed .idx.gz oracle's OR-blit background is capturable on the trace core, and the only capturable frame (gy=118) has no committed .idx.gz oracle. A 100% full-viewport gate would require EITHER bridging the two cores' serialize formats (so the trace core can load the committed gy=121 state) OR a deterministic from-on-disk-asset placement-table generator (below) that needs no live capture.

findings.claim: The PER-VIEW placement-list selection (how the engine fills cs:[0x190]/cs:[0x18e] for a given zone/facing/geometry) is the next-task generalization and the deterministic route to a from-asset 100% gate that needs NO live capture. The current ported decoder consumes a RESOLVED BackgroundPlacement[] (the asm's per-image si/di/cx/w/h/planeStride + the 4-plane planar source). To generate that list from the committed on-disk assets: (1) decode the floor (zone0 id 1346) / ceiling (id 1740) / window assets via the already-cracked .pic RLE decoder into the 4-plane planar work-buffer layout the descriptor table references (validate the on-disk-sourced sub-images reproduce the live in-RAM work buffers); (2) read the FULL cs:[0x18e] image-descriptor + cs:[0x190] placement tables (statically from ega.drv or live at the relocated base) and determine the per-view selection index (the perspective-triangle / black-void / window geometry as a function of (zone, facing, depth)). With (1)+(2) the placement list is GENERATED deterministically (like the wall span/flush generator), and composeBackground reproduces ANY committed frame's background WITHOUT a live OR-blit capture — sidestepping the trace-core frame-capture blocker entirely. THIS is the recommended path to the first full-viewport byte-exact gate.

evidence.details: Tables: PLACEMENT @cs:[0x190] (5-byte recs {imageIdx,destX,destRow,bias,count}), IMAGE-descriptor @cs:[0x18e] (5-byte recs {segDelta,srcOff,w,h}); source seg base cs:[0x149], page seg cs:[0x14d].
